data.title: RAG
data.tagline: A method that retrieves relevant passages from specified material at answer time and gives them to the model
data.learningOutcome: You can check whether material is ready, what passage was actually retrieved, and whether the answer is supported.
data.description: When customer support answers a refund question, RAG first finds relevant passages in connected policy material and then lets the model answer from them. New material must finish processing and enter the searchable set before later answers can use it; retrieval may still miss a passage or the model may misread it.

learning.assumes: You know AI can answer questions and have seen it use company documents.
learning.outcome: You can check whether material is ready, what passage was actually retrieved, and whether the answer is supported.

distinctions.label: Fine-tuning
distinctions.explanation: Fine-tuning continues training a model with examples; RAG retrieves external material when answering. A policy change usually requires updating and processing the retrieval material, not retraining the model.

distinctions.label: Pasting material into a question
distinctions.explanation: Pasting material supplies what the model should read for that request; RAG searches connected material for passages based on the question. Neither guarantees the model will understand correctly.

explanation.title: Completion is a prerequisite
explanation.text: After a file changes, its search index may still be processing. Completion makes the material available to search; it does not promise every query will find the right passage.

explanation.title: Compare the answer with its source
explanation.text: Check whether the retrieved passage supports the reply. Missed passages, outdated material, or a model misreading the source can still lead to an inaccurate answer.

data.boundary: RAG gives retrieved material to a model as a reference. It does not guarantee the right passage is found, understood, or followed.

lessonPractice.title: The refund policy was just edited, its file still says “processing,” and AI cites the old rule. What should you check first?

options.label: Wait for processing to finish, ask again, and inspect the passage retrieved
options.feedback: Correct. New content may not be in the searchable set while processing is underway; after it completes, confirm the new clause was actually retrieved.

options.label: Rewrite the question to emphasize “use the latest rule”
options.feedback: A clearer question can help, but it does not put an unprocessed file into retrieval results.

options.label: Retrain the model on the new policy so it remembers the refund rule
options.feedback: That changes model training; for an external policy update, first confirm the retrieval material finished processing and was found.

data.agentPrompt: I just updated the refund policy. First confirm that the file has finished processing, then ask the same question and inspect the retrieved passage and answer citation. Tell me if it still finds the old rule or no relevant passage.
